title: How to Order Currywurst in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **Mit Darm** is a sausage in a pork casing that snaps; **ohne Darm** has no casing and is softer and paler.
**Ohne Darm is the older Berlin style.** Curry 36 says the 1950s Berlin currywurst was a scalded sausage without casing.
**A full order:** "Einmal Currywurst ohne Darm, scharf, mit Pommes rot-weiß, bitte."
**Say nothing about heat and you get house normal**, which is mild. Scharf is hot, extra scharf is very hot.
**Pommes rot-weiß** is fries with ketchup and mayo. A **Schrippe** is the plain Berlin bread roll.
**Hier** means you eat at the counter, **zum Mitnehmen** means to take away.
**Konnopke's sells only ohne Darm** and is closed on Sundays and Mondays.
**Curry 36 serves both kinds**, so it is the easy place to compare them.
